title: Distance From Prime Meridian Calculator
description: Measure your distance from the prime meridian with the Distance From Prime Meridian Calculator — New York 6,036 km west of Greenwich's line. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, London itself is only 8.8 km west of the prime meridian at its latitude — while New York is 6,036 km away, roughly a quarter of the way around the world.
quick_answer: The Distance From Prime Meridian Calculator measures the surface distance from your point to the prime meridian — the 0 degrees longitude line through Greenwich. Enter a place and read how far east or west of the world's zero line you stand.

body.t: Standing on the line at Greenwich is the photo; this calculator tells everyone else how far their photo would have to travel. The line's finder page:
Distance from the meridian tracks solar-time difference: ~1,670 km at the equator per hour of longitude (15°). The clock version lives in the time-zone tools.
Longitude stops being an abstract angle when it is 6,036 km of ocean and continent between you and a brass strip in London.
Chronometers, the 1884 conference, the longitude problem — all of it was about measuring this distance at sea.
Computed great-circle distance from New York to the meridian (crossing at New York's latitude): 6,036.2 km. The same figure for Chicago is 6,900.8 km — America's interior is a long way from zero.

GPS zero (the IERS Reference Meridian) passes about 102 m east of the famous Airy transit circle at Greenwich — satellites re-surveyed what 1851 brass could not. On this calculator's scale, both are simply 'the line'.

popular_table.note: The shortest route to a meridian is a great circle that meets it at right angles — for most places it runs close to (slightly poleward of) your own parallel.

faq: The 1884 International Meridian Conference chose Greenwich — already the reference for most charts and the 0° of the dominant almanac — by vote. Paris kept its own meridian on maps for decades after.
East or west — does it say which?
Yes: the sign of your longitude is the answer, and the result reports the side. The distance itself is the same either way.
The shortest surface distance to the line — for latitude lines that is the meridian arc; for the prime meridian it is the great-circle route to the nearest point of the meridian.
Does terrain or sea level matter?
No — distances are surface geometry on the reference sphere; mountains do not shorten the way to a latitude line.
Stand on the line and it is: the tropics and circles have real ground you can occupy, and the result honours it.
Sphere-accurate to well under a kilometre for these magnitudes — plenty for education, planning and curiosity; geodesists refine with the ellipsoid.
Signs and hemispheres are handled — a southern point measures to southern lines by the same geometry.
